applicableAreas: southern boundary of site, adjacent to Valley View Road
findings.comment: Live Oak trees (Quercus Virginiana) shown on landscape plan approximately 5-7 feet north of overhead electric line along southern property boundary. Live Oak is a large tree species with mature height 40-60+ feet, requiring minimum 25-foot clearance from distribution conductors. Trees are planted well within prohibited zone with no documented Austin Energy approval.

applicableAreas: southern boundary of site near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not include a plant legend identifying the species of trees depicted near the overhead electric line. While Sheet 35 provides a plant schedule cross-reference, the landscape plan itself lacks species identification, preventing direct verification of utility compatibility and clearance compliance on the drawing.

applicableAreas: landscape plan throughout site, specifically trees near overhead utilities
findings.comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated from small trees on the landscape plan. No notation, symbol distinction, or legend entry indicates which proposed trees will mature to 40+ feet, preventing verification of compliance with 25-foot clearance requirements from distribution conductors and other specified restrictions.

applicableAreas: southern boundary of site, adjacent to Valley View Road
findings.comment: Trees (Live Oak and/or Cedar Elm) are proposed within prohibited clearance zones (less than 25 feet from distribution conductors for large trees and/or less than 15 feet for distribution facilities generally). No documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing these exceptions is evident on the site plan, in notes, or in attached correspondence.

applicableAreas: southern boundary of site near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Tree species proposed near overhead distribution facilities cannot be verified as utility-compatible without access to ECM Appendix F UC designation column. While plant schedule identifies species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm), their UC status cannot be confirmed from available site plan documents.

Specific utility pole locations are not clearly marked on the landscape plan. While an overhead electric line is shown, individual pole positions are not labeled, preventing verification of whether any trees are planted within 10 feet of poles. Utility Plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical infrastructure but is not cross-referenced on landscape plan for pole location verification.

Pad-mounted electric equipment locations shown on Electrical Plan (Sheet 21) are not cross-referenced on or depicted on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Clearance distances between proposed trees and pad-mount transformers and access doors cannot be verified without composite view of both plans.

Underground electric equipment (pull boxes, other utility vaults) depicted on Electrical Plan (Sheet 21) are not cross-referenced on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Distances between proposed trees and underground equipment cannot be verified to confirm 5-foot minimum clearance requirements.

Whether any trees are proposed within 20 feet of underground electric equipment cannot be determined from available plans without composite reference. Landscape plan does not depict underground equipment locations. No root barrier specifications or details are shown on landscape plan for any trees that might require them per code.

applicableAreas: southern boundary of site near overhead electric line
findings.comment: No clearance dimension lines are present on the landscape plan indicating distances between trees and the overhead electric line. Without dimensions, the reference point (pole centerline vs. outer conductor) cannot be verified. Grouping notes that conductors are offset 4+ feet laterally from pole center; measurement methodology cannot be confirmed absent from any clearance callouts.

applicableAreas: southern boundary of site near overhead electric line
findings.comment: No clearance dimension lines or callouts are shown on the landscape plan between trees and the overhead electric line. Without dimensions, verification of whether measurements originate from tree trunk center (correct) or from projected canopy edge (incorrect) cannot be performed.
